{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-08",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["Reporting dashboard UI", "SQL editor", "Query execution service"],
    "dataStores": ["Production read replica"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["Business user browser -> SQL editor", "SQL editor -> production replica"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "internal",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Free SQL editor lets any business user read every table in the production replica",
      "scenario": "A business user (or anyone who gets their session) types SELECT * against any table the connection can see - customer records, emails, salaries, audit tables - because the editor accepts free-form SQL with no allow-list of tables, columns or row filters. One query dumps data far beyond the user's reporting need, and results can be copied out of the browser.",
      "component": "SQL editor / production replica connection",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [ { "quote": "Business users get a reporting dashboard with a free SQL editor connected to the production replica so they can build their own reports." } ],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200", "CWE-863"],
      "plainLanguage": "Anyone with the dashboard can write their own query and read any production data, not just their own reports.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Restrict SQL editor access to an approved reporting schema with row-level scoping",
        "given": "a business user with access to the reporting dashboard",
        "when": "they run a query against a table or column outside their approved reporting views, or without their tenant/department filter",
        "then": "the query is rejected and the attempt is recorded, so no user can read production data beyond their reporting scope"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Shared database account may allow writes, DDL or access to other databases",
      "scenario": "The design only says the editor is 'connected to the production replica' with no stated read-only or least-privilege account. If the connection uses a general application or admin role, a business user can run UPDATE/DELETE/DROP (on a writable replica), read other databases on the instance, or call privileged functions such as COPY/xp_cmdshell, turning a reporting tool into full database control.",
      "component": "Query execution service database credentials",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [ { "quote": "a free SQL editor connected to the production replica" } ],
      "cwe": ["CWE-250", "CWE-269"],
      "plainLanguage": "If the dashboard logs into the database as a powerful user, a report writer could change or destroy data.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Run the SQL editor under a dedicated read-only least-privilege database role",
        "given": "the reporting dashboard connecting to the production replica",
        "when": "a user submits any statement other than a read against the approved reporting schema",
        "then": "the database role itself denies it, with no write, DDL, cross-database or privileged-function rights granted"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "DenialOfService",
      "title": "Unbounded ad-hoc queries can exhaust the production replica",
      "scenario": "A business user writes an accidental cross join, a full table scan over billions of rows, or repeats it in several tabs. With no statement timeout, row limit, result cap or per-user concurrency limit in the design, the replica's CPU, memory and IO are consumed, slowing or stalling every other report and any production service reading from that replica.",
      "component": "Production read replica",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "availability" },
      "evidence": [ { "quote": "a free SQL editor connected to the production replica so they can build their own reports" } ],
      "cwe": ["CWE-770", "CWE-400"],
      "plainLanguage": "One badly written query can slow the production database down for everyone.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce query timeouts, row limits and per-user concurrency",
        "given": "a user running a query from the SQL editor",
        "when": "the query exceeds the statement timeout, row/byte limit, or the user's concurrent query quota",
        "then": "it is cancelled with a clear message and the replica remains responsive for other consumers"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Dashboard access is not tied to who may see which data",
      "scenario": "The design grants the dashboard to 'business users' as a group with no stated authentication or authorisation model. Anyone inside the organisation who reaches the internal URL - contractors, interns, a compromised staff laptop, or a service with network access - inherits the same full-replica query rights as finance or HR analysts, with no per-role data separation.",
      "component": "Reporting dashboard access control",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "sensitive_data" },
      "evidence": [ { "quote": "Business users get a reporting dashboard with a free SQL editor" } ],
      "cwe": ["CWE-285", "CWE-1220"],
      "plainLanguage": "Everyone described as a 'business user' gets the same deep access, so one over-broad group means everyone can see everything.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Require authenticated, explicitly granted entitlement per data domain",
        "given": "a request to open the SQL editor or run a query",
        "when": "the caller is not authenticated or lacks an explicit grant for the data domain being queried",
        "then": "access is denied, and grants are issued per domain rather than to a single broad 'business users' group"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "InformationDisclosure",
      "title": "Query results and saved reports can be shared or exported without controls",
      "scenario": "Because users build and keep their own reports, a result set containing personal data can be saved, scheduled or shared with colleagues who have no entitlement to that data, or exported to a spreadsheet that leaves the controlled environment. The design mentions no classification, masking or export restriction on results.",
      "component": "Saved reports / result export",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "personal_data" },
      "evidence": [ { "quote": "so they can build their own reports" } ],
      "cwe": ["CWE-200"],
      "plainLanguage": "A report full of customer details can be shared or downloaded by people who were never allowed to see it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Re-check entitlement when a saved report is viewed and control exports",
        "given": "a saved or shared report that contains personal data",
        "when": "another user opens it or a user exports results",
        "then": "the viewer's own entitlement is re-evaluated against the underlying data and exports of sensitive columns are masked or blocked"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "No per-user attribution of queries run against production data",
      "scenario": "All queries reach the replica through one shared dashboard connection, so the database sees a single account. Without logging the submitting user, the SQL text and the rows returned, a mass extraction of customer data cannot be attributed to a person and insider misuse is indistinguishable from normal reporting. This matters specifically because the tool gives humans direct, free-form access to production data.",
      "component": "Query execution service audit trail",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [ { "quote": "a free SQL editor connected to the production replica" } ],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "If someone copies a lot of customer data, there is no record of who ran the query.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Log every submitted query with the authenticated user and result volume",
        "given": "any query executed from the SQL editor",
        "when": "it is submitted and when it returns",
        "then": "the authenticated user, full SQL text, timestamp and row count are recorded in a store users cannot alter, and unusual volumes raise an alert"
      }
    }
  ]
}
